name: Almost Regular Bracket Sequence
description: You are given a bracket sequence $$$s$$$ consisting of $$$n$$$ opening ' ( ' and closing ' ) ' brackets. A regular bracket sequence is a bracket sequence that can be transformed into a correct arithmetic expression by inserting characters ' 1 ' and ' + ' between the original characters of the sequence. For example, bracket sequences " ()() ", " (()) " are regular (the resulting expressions are: " (1)+(1) ", " ((1+1)+1) "), and " )( " and " ( " are not. You can change the type of some bracket $$$s_i$$$. It means that if $$$s_i = $$$ ' ) ' then you can change it to ' ( ' and vice versa. Your task is to calculate the number of positions $$$i$$$ such that if you change the type of the $$$i$$$-th bracket, then the resulting bracket sequence becomes regular .
input_specification: The first line of the input contains one integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 10^6$$$) — the length of the bracket sequence. The second line of the input contains the string $$$s$$$ consisting of $$$n$$$ opening ' ( ' and closing ' ) ' brackets.
output_specification: Print one integer — the number of positions $$$i$$$ such that if you change the type of the $$$i$$$-th bracket, then the resulting bracket sequence becomes regular .
approach_summary: Identify exchange argument or greedy choice property. Sort elements by payoff ratio or deadline and greedily pick candidates to achieve global optimum.
